terms.meaning: a pop-up window that sits above the page and asks for attention
the dimmed cover placed behind a dialog so the page behind looks inactive
a way of drawing an element at the top level of the page so it is not clipped by layouts beneath it

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Dialog box, cover and header
sections.what: Sets up the dimmed cover over the page, the centered white box that holds the message, and the header area for the title. The box fades and zooms in when it opens.
sections.why: Gives every confirmation pop-up the same placement and feel.
sections.watch_out: The cover and the placement are added automatically inside the content part, so a page should not add its own cover.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Footer, title, text and confirm button
sections.what: Sets the footer layout, which stacks buttons on phones and places them side by side on larger screens. It also styles the title, the grey description text and the confirm button.
sections.why: The confirm button borrows the shared button look so it matches the rest of the app.
sections.watch_out: The confirm button uses the default style, so a risky action such as deleting needs a different style from the page.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Cancel button and exports
sections.what: Styles the cancel button as an outline button and adds space above it on phones. Then it makes all the dialog parts available to other files.
sections.why: Likely reason: cancel is styled more quietly than confirm so the main choice stands out. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Replacing the cancel part with a plain button would lose the closing and focus behavior the Radix library provides.

summary: A set of styled pop-up confirmation dialogs with a title, a message, a confirm button and a cancel button.
purpose: Lets a page ask the user to confirm an important action, such as deleting something, before it happens.
why: Likely reason: a shared dialog so every confirmation in the app looks the same and uses the same button styles. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Step 1: Loads the Radix alert dialog behavior and the shared button styles. Step 2: Builds the dark background cover, the centered box, and the header. Step 3: Builds the footer, title, description and confirm button. Step 4: Builds the cancel button and exports every part.
inputs: Title and description text, the confirm and cancel buttons placed inside the dialog, plus any extra style classes.
outputs: A centered pop-up box over a dimmed page, with confirm and cancel buttons. Choosing either closes the dialog.
risks: The source for one long style string is cut off in this packet, so its full styling could not be read. The confirm button uses the default style, so a dangerous action needs its style changed by the page.
debug: If the dialog does not appear, check that the page uses the trigger and content parts inside the root part. If the buttons look wrong, check that the shared button file is present and that the page overrides nothing unexpected. If the layout stacks wrongly on phones, check the footer classes.
